title: HIDEOUT
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Seiichi, a failing novelist whose life was upended by a family tragedy his wife Miki blames him for, takes her to a remote island planning to kill her. When he chases her into a cave, they find it inhabited by something that thrives in the dark, and the hunt turns into a fight for survival. A one-volume horror story about marital hatred and the ugliest parts of human nature.
life_message: It holds up no ideal so much as warning: grief and hatred left to fester turn people into monsters.

Sustained claustrophobic horror and a premeditated murder plot (ComicsBeat; Horror genre; AniList Survival).
Grief after a family tragedy curdles into murderous intent (ComicsBeat; AniList Tragedy; Psychological genre).
A husband plots to kill his wife (ComicsBeat).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Seiichi answers blame with private violence rather than any outside remedy.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Isolated island and cave place characters beyond law.

Civic vs kin.evidence: The drama is entirely within a family and its wounds.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: No social hierarchy in play; a struggle between spouses.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: No religious or customary frame; raw human psychology.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Pure survival in the dark dominates.

folkways.japan: The writer protagonist and the pressures of failure and household blame echo Japanese literary horror and family-shame themes.

delivery.evidence: Summaries frame it as a horror story about hatred born of grief, withholding sympathy from everyone; no comment on preachiness found (to verify).
delivery.note: Its warning about festering grief and hatred is carried by the plot and left for the reader to judge.

winners_losers: No one truly wins; Seiichi's hatred and the cave's predation consume. Sympathy is withheld from everyone, leaving the reader to judge.
